Show that the sequence $\\left(f_{n}\\right)$ does not converge uniformly.", "assumptions": [], "domain": "topology", "explicit_subgoals": []}, "target": {"node_id": "n2", "version": 1}, "target_node": {"text": "The sequence $\\left(f_n\\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\\varepsilon<1$ and $N \\in \\mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\\left(f_N(x), f(x)\\right)=\\varepsilon$.", "claim": "Claims nonuniform convergence by choosing, for each positive integer $N$ and $0<\\varepsilon<1$, the point $x=\\varepsilon^{1/N}$. The calculation requires the unstated pointwise limit $f(x)=0$ for $x<1$; fixing one such $\\varepsilon$, for example $1/2$, would then match the negation of uniform convergence.", "scope": [], "depends_on": []}, "closed_predecessors": [], "base_state_digest": "81e17daa5d6964edfa4f1f733447e8e0a5ed8ad8338736ce6a0d6a5646c7b917", "certificate": {"certificate_id": "3505c990c3ce2692989bd4759c1ac02362457a7ee76f45dc63e2e390e9c87073", "problem_digest": "e5fcea369deb30b6c131db77aba1a1b879c1171eb489f4427aebc25df4006bda", "target": {"node_id": "n2", "version": 1}, "graph_digest": "1dfa4bf8d15529f66a4ffbb2f1bb3884aba7bf42aaa2f5dd7ccf128d4f1ac463", "confirmation": "confirmed", "kind": "gap", "failed_edge": "No predecessor establishes the function f or the pointwise limit of (f_n), yet the conclusion uses f(x) and its value at x=ε^(1/N).", "quote": "The sequence $\\left(f_n\\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\\varepsilon<1$ and $N \\in \\mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\\left(f_N(x), f(x)\\right)=\\varepsilon$.", "reason": "The equality is unsupported because $f$ is undefined. One must first establish the pointwise limit $f(x)=0$ for $x<1$ and $f(1)=1$. Then, for any fixed $\\varepsilon_0\\in(0,1)$ and every $N$, choosing $n=N$ and $x=\\varepsilon_0^{1/N}<1$ gives $|f_N(x)-f(x)|=\\varepsilon_0$, which negates uniform convergence. The wording “given ε” can supply such a fixed ε, so the essential gap is the missing definition and justification of $f$."}, "limits": {"max_new_nodes_per_patch": 2, "max_total_node_edits": 6}}
